Multi-Star Industrial Coordination Engine. Plans resource allocation and research across star systems that operate with long delays and partial independence.

This database covers the technology as item 214 entry 36 of Manon's "100 Technologies Beyond Omega (A)" catalog, section "Interstellar Engineering". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

body:
Known science foundations of Multi-Star Industrial Coordination Engine.

Global supply chains coordinate across continents. Space agencies plan multi-mission campaigns. But year-long delays force full local independence; the 'coordination engine' is a planning concept for a future with no present users.

Key quantity check (Star systems with industry / star systems known): computed ratio 5e-12 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.5. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Multi-Star Industrial Coordination Engine - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Plans resource allocation and research across star systems that operate with long delays and partial independence.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Multi-Star Industrial Coordination Engine.

No multi-star industry exists. Delays force autonomy; coordination adds little. The engine plans for users that do not exist.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 11.3 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is industrial systems vs known systems at 11.3 orders of magnitude (known systems larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
